The source Proposition 3.1 provides delta_j=u_epsilon,j-alpha_j=epsilon^gamma(w_j+r_epsilon,j) with ||r_epsilon,j||_infty->0 and mean(w_j)=0. Thus mean(delta_j^2)=epsilon^(2 gamma)(mean(w_j^2)+o(1)) and mean(delta_j^3)=O(epsilon^(3 gamma))=o(epsilon^(2 gamma)). The exact cubic Taylor identity gives 0=g_prime(alpha)mean(delta)+0.5 g_doubleprime(alpha)mean(delta^2)+b mean(delta^3); dividing by the assumed nonzero g_prime(alpha) yields the claimed formula. Sympy independently checked the polynomial expansion and simplification (3b alpha+c)/(3b alpha^2+2c alpha+d). This is a valid p>2, epsilon->0+ asymptotic on any local solution family with the source leading profile; no uniqueness or finite-experiment extrapolation is used.
